newsitem.title: JAPAN: US would worry if Japan surplus trends up - official.
newsitem.headline: US would worry if Japan surplus trends up - official.

text.p: The United States would be concerned if data for Japan's January current account surplus, released earlier on Thursday, indicated a "trend upward", a U.S. government official said.
"If this indicates a trend upward, then it would be a matter of concern to us, as Deputy Treasury Secretary (Lawrence) Summers made clear," the official told Reuters by telephone.
"Clearly the reduction (in the current account surplus) has bottomed out, so there is concern that it might be headed back up," the official added.

The Finance Ministry announced on Thursday morning that Japan's surplus in its current account, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, rose sharply in January to an unadjusted 150.7 billion yen from 32.6 billion a year earlier. Many economists had forecast a deficit.
Summers, in a speech last Friday and again in a news conference in Tokyo on Tuesday, urged Japan to make sure its recovery was led by domestic growth and that its trade surplus did not surge.
He also said Japan may need to take extra fiscal, financial and deregulatory steps to ensure those objectives are met.

U.S. officials have become particularly worried that Tokyo's plans to reduce its budget deficit, including a rise in its sales tax in April, could further undermine growth and hence lead to a resurgence of its current account and trade surpluses.
